items.title: Claude Williams interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995
items.q: When I was over in London last year or the year before last I was following him. Like Grappelli would play here this week and he’d move on and I’d play there.

ctx.x: Do you think there are violinists that try to copy your style?

Well it’s a few violin players that, oh there’s a lot of good violin players that I consider better than me now, but it’s a different style. Like Grappelli plays a beautiful fiddle. When I was over in London last year or the year before last I was following him. Like Grappelli would play here this week and he’d move on and I’d play there. So they would say, “You know Grappelli plays pretty but I’d rather hear you.” You know, my style was still different.
I wanted to ask you a little bit more about the Kansas City scene. Can you tell us how it changed from the 30s going into the 40s and the 40s to the 50s?
